entries.retired_scope: Spark or another hosted wallet as the custody layer for agents.

evidence.summary: Episode triage records the move from Spark custody to the self-custodial MoneyDevKit and LDK stack.

current.violated_principle: Agents and users retain custody; hosted custody must not become a platform dependency.
current.replacement_path: Use the MoneyDevKit and LDK self-custodial wallet stack.
current.reconsideration_trigger: A self-custodial Spark design with production evidence and no hosted custody dependency.

entries.retired_scope: A NIP-90 data-vending-machine market without a named buyer and working product.

evidence.summary: Seller-first markets and protocol-only launches did not establish durable buyer demand.

current.violated_principle: Name the buyer and ship usable software before creating a market protocol.
current.replacement_path: Use the accepted-outcome economy for a verified demand path with a named buyer.
current.reconsideration_trigger: A committed buyer, executable product flow, and paid end-to-end transaction.

entries.retired_scope: GetAfter as a second source-control forge.

evidence.summary: The OpenAgents forge replaced the shelved GetAfter alternative.

current.violated_principle: One canonical forge owns source control and work state.
current.replacement_path: Extend the OpenAgents forge instead of operating a second forge.
current.reconsideration_trigger: A legally or operationally mandatory isolation boundary the current forge cannot provide.

entries.retired_scope: Paying providers for online presence, uptime, or unverified mining.

evidence.summary: Episode 224 retired presence-based rewards in favor of verified machine-learning work.

current.violated_principle: Settle verified outcomes, not claimed availability.
current.replacement_path: Pay against accepted work receipts with verification and settlement evidence.
current.reconsideration_trigger: A fraud-resistant proof that presence itself creates measurable buyer value.

current.violated_principle: Executor targets must expose controllable lifecycle, evidence, and recovery contracts.
current.replacement_path: Use the Codex, OpenCode, Probe, and owned computer-execution paths.
current.reconsideration_trigger: Copilot exposes the lifecycle, evidence, and recovery contracts required by the fleet.

entries.retired_scope: A monolithic all-in-one business operating system.
match_phrases: single business operating system for everything

evidence.summary: Current plans organize work as composable issue, project, execution, receipt, and settlement surfaces.

current.violated_principle: Compose bounded products around the accepted-outcome loop instead of centralizing every business function.
current.replacement_path: Build interoperable forge, fleet, verification, receipt, and settlement capabilities.
current.reconsideration_trigger: Repeated user evidence that a bounded integration cannot satisfy a specific workflow.

entries.retired_scope: Claude Code or another rival-owned runtime as a hard platform dependency.

evidence.summary: The Anthropic OAuth cutoff demonstrated the failure mode of a rival-owned runtime dependency.

current.violated_principle: OpenAgents must retain runtime portability and control of critical execution paths.
current.replacement_path: Keep rival runtimes behind optional adapters and maintain owned or multi-provider execution paths.
current.reconsideration_trigger: A portable open contract with an interchangeable implementation and no vendor-controlled authentication dependency.
